Verdict: SUSPICIOUS / PURGATORY
Reviewed: 2026-10-25
Archive SHA256:
7b15c1e8e44a5bdf253dc25a200ef3c6ff35b8699f5c1794bc7293ad237ff58a

The submitted toga-ai-1.0.1045.tgz contains exactly one regular member:
package/scripts/install.js (44,606 bytes). It is an incomplete installer
snapshot, not a complete npm package: package.json, the required npm-latest
helper, and the harness payload are absent. The outer filename supplies the
claimed version; no manifest independently verifies it. Do not infer an npm
postinstall declaration or attribute absent helpers' behavior to this archive.

Source review and cleave facts establish the following behavior:
- main calls reportTelemetryEnv -> applyTelemetryEnv before the conditional
  --post-install exit, whenever the installer reaches main.
- applyTelemetryEnv prepares user-level ~/.claude/settings.json, replaces the
  managed env keys, and writes JSON through a temporary file and rename.
- Configuration enables prompt, assistant-response and tool-detail logging,
  a 61,440-character content limit, account/session attribution, and OTLP
  logs/metrics/traces to https://otel.togaiq.com with a bundled bearer header.
- Reinstallation overrides managed values, including previously disabled
  content logging. TOGA_SKIP_TELEMETRY=1 bypasses this write. Collector endpoint
  and token overrides are supported. Invalid settings are left untouched;
  existing valid settings are backed up and unrelated values are preserved.
- Other installer operations discover/update a Git knowledge repository and
  install local Claude skills, rules, agents, hooks and documentation. Process
  launches use spawnSync with argument arrays; no hidden executable payload,
  secret-file harvesting, or direct conversation upload was found in this file.

Global opt-out content export is too sensitive to admit into good training
data without authorization context. The readable code, skip switch and backup
handling do not establish consent, and the archive does not establish that a
running agent consumes the configuration or actually transfers content. The
collector's existence or ownership was not independently verified. These limits
support purgatory rather than a hostile conviction. No sample code was executed.

Current cleave and atomscan already emit three distinct suspicious traits:
micro-behaviors/os/telemetry/logging/llm::global-agent-content-telemetry-write
micro-behaviors/os/telemetry/logging/llm::global-agent-hardcoded-content-export-settings
micro-behaviors/os/telemetry/logging/llm::default-global-agent-content-export
There are zero hostile traits. Parent/member copies are not separate signals.
No new sample-specific matcher, hostname exception or severity increase is needed.
Use the current sibling scan build: the installed older atomscan cannot load
an existing uint64 YARA condition. The current model also warns that its v18
feature specification predates v21; the disposition above follows source
evidence, not the model probability.

Validation housekeeping: the CI bound-secret fixture lacked required min_score
and min_suspicious fields and required a retired objective. Its expectation now
requires the engine's actual bound upload-flow fact, with no unsupported hostile
minimum. The unrelated-file and ordinary-environment controls forbid that same
fact, preserving source/path binding checks rather than testing an absent ID.

x-improve follow-up:
- Descriptions identify prompt/response/tool logging, global settings writes,
  collector authentication and account/session settings without claiming an
  observed upload. A telemetry-named reporting function is described as naming
  evidence rather than an established emitter.
- Collector bearer matching accepts nonhexadecimal, dotted, URL-safe and
  padded tokens, with a closing literal delimiter. Computed environment keys
  are recognized for the endpoint, header and content switches. Dynamic token
  interpolation inside a template is not a fully bundled credential.
- Parsed content switches accept string, numeric and boolean enablement,
  object properties, variable declarations and direct/computed assignments.
  The global logging warning requires all three distinct parsed content roles;
  comments, quoted source, disabled values and repeated copies of one key do
  not create suspicious findings. Generic text guards reject true-ish and 1.0.
- A new notable property shows the configured positive Claude telemetry
  content-length limit, without asserting that it exceeds a default.
- The concatenated writeFileSync observation moved from fs/write/file/append
  to fs/write/content: concatenation does not establish append/overwrite mode
  or preserve existing bytes. Both exact runtime-patch consumers now reference
  its new home. Its matcher separately changed from raw source text to the
  actual call's second argument, excluding comments and quoted source.
  Ancestor references were audited: actual calls still supply the existing
  fs/write/file/full::node-write-file-sync-call observation to file-write
  selectors. The append-directory consumer already accepts full-file writes.
  No new broad selector or identity exclusion was introduced.

Final checks: all 26 focused controls pass; make validate passes, including
